q: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a constant acceleration $g$.
e: This is the foundational assumption for freely falling bodies near the earth's surface.

q: If the air resistance is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall.
e: This is the exact definition of free fall provided in the text.

q: Equations of motion under constant acceleration described in chapter 2 cannot be used in free fall.
e: Equations of motion under constant acceleration can be used in free fall.

q: In free fall equations, we will use the symbol $h$ for displacement $s$ and $g$ for acceleration $a$.
e: This is the specific notation adaptation for free fall problems.

q: The equations of motion for free fall become $v = v_0 + gt$, $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2gh$, and $h = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
e: These are the correct adapted kinematic equations for free fall.

q: The acceleration due to gravity $g$ is directed upwards (away from the centre of the earth).
e: The acceleration due to gravity $g$ is directed downwards (towards the centre of the earth).

q: The value of $g$ varies only slightly from one place to another, and therefore, its value is assumed to be constant in the calculations.
e: This justifies treating $g$ as a constant in standard free fall problems.

q: Displacement $h$ will be positive if it is below the origin and negative above the origin.
e: Displacement $h$ will be positive if it is above the origin and negative below the origin.

q: Velocities $v_0$ and $v$ will be positive if they are directed upward and negative if directed downward.
e: This is the sign convention for velocity in the one-dimensional coordinate system described.

q: Since acceleration $g$ is always directed downwards, its value will be negative (i.e., $g = -9.8 \text{ m s}^{-2}$).
e: This follows the established sign convention where downward is negative.

q: In solving free fall problems, we use a one-dimensional coordinate system with its origin taken as the initial position of the body under consideration.
e: This is the standard setup for solving the free fall equations presented.
